unit.why: A single narrative: the Maggid of Mezeritch sends R. Nahum of Chernobyl to R. Aaron of Karlin's grave to announce a soul from the world of tikkun, which is then born as R. Mordechai (Motele) of Chernobyl, who marries R. Aaron's daughter.
unit.boundary_note: Ends with the source abbreviation 'מתו'' (truncated attribution).

stories.start_quote: הרה״מ הק' אמר כ״פ לתלמידיו הקדושים
stories.summary_en: The Maggid of Mezeritch holds a great soul from the world of tikkun. After R. Aaron of Karlin dies, he sends R. Nahum of Chernobyl to the grave to announce that this soul will be born to Nahum as a son who will marry Aaron's little daughter Haya Sarah; R. Motele of Chernobyl is born that year and marries her.

tags.why: The story is about the destined birth of R. Motele of Chernobyl from a special soul.
The Maggid predicts the birth and the marriage, and both come true.
